akhfash:18-18.t: He said ﴿قَوْماً بُوراً﴾: the plural of "البَائِر" (one who perishes), like "اليَهُود" (the Jews), whose singular is "الهَائِد". Some said: "It is a usage not based on a singular, as is said 'أَنْتَ بَشَرٌ' (you are a human) and 'أَنْتُمْ بَشَر' (you are humans)."

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفاً وَلاَ نَصْراً﴾: He omitted "from the disbelievers". It may also be about the angels. The proof that it is addressed to the disbelievers is that He said ﴿وَمَن يَظْلِم مِّنكُمْ﴾. Some said: "He means the angels."

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿ٱلَّتِيۤ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾: two dialect forms; one says "مُطِرْنَا" and "أُمْطِرْنَا" (we were rained upon). And He said ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً﴾; they are two dialect forms.

akhfash:49-49.t: And He said ﴿وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً﴾ with a doubled (yāʾ), because it is the plural of "الإِنْسِيّ" (human being).

akhfash:57-57.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the speech, in the meaning of "لكنّ" (but).

akhfash:62-62.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾: He means "they succeed one another".

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: this has no khabar (predicate) except in meaning, and Allah knows best.

akhfash:74-74.t:
And He said ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً﴾: "الإِمام" (leader) here is plural, as He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ﴾. It may also be by way of quotation, as a man says, when asked "مَنْ أميرُكُم" (who is your commander?): "هؤلاءِ أَمِيرُنا" (these are our commander). The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 255]:
يَا عَاذِلاَتِي لا تُرِدْنَ مَلامَتي * إِنَّ العَواذِلَ لَيْسَ لِي بِأَمِير
(O my reproachers, do not seek to blame me; the reproachers are no commander over me.)

akhfash:77-77.t: And He said ﴿مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ﴾ because it is from "عَبَأْتُ بِهِ" (I cared about him), "أَنّا أَعْبَأُ بِهِ" "عَبْأً".

daas-irab:43-44.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is interrogative, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa); the meaning of أرأيت is "tell me". ﴿مَنِ﴾ a relative noun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of رأيت. ﴿اتَّخَذَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلهَهُ﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi, placed first, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هَواهُ﴾ the first mafʿūl bihi, placed later; the second mafʿūl bihi was put first because it is more important. ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ﴾ the hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted. ﴿أنت﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَكُونُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) وكيلا, and the noun (ism) of تكون is omitted. ﴿وَكِيلًا﴾ the khabar (predicate) of تكون; the clause ﴿تَكُونُ..﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت, and the clause ﴿أنت..﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi of أرأيت. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَحْسَبُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil necessarily latent. ﴿أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ أنّ and its noun, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; أنّ together with its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of تحسب. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of أنّ. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يسمعون. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle of negation. [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿أَنَّ﴾ here; the Quranic word is إِنْ (إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ), the negating particle being described.] ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كَالْأَنْعامِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾ khabar. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is conjoined to the first «هم أضل». [Translator's note: presumably the first clause «هم كالأنعام» is meant.]

daas-irab:45-47.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for affirmative interrogation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and لم is a jussive particle. ﴿تَرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَدَّ الظِّلَّ﴾ a past verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for the kāf. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿شاءَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَجَعَلَهُ﴾ the lām is the one occurring in the apodosis (jawāb) of لو, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis of لولا with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: «لولا» in the source is evidently «لو لا», i.e. "of لو, with no grammatical position".] ﴿ساكِناً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا الشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دليلا; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْناهُ إِلَيْنا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً﴾ a past verb, fāʿil, mafʿūl bihi, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and an adjective (naʿt) qualifying it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the relative noun is its khabar (predicate); the wāw is resumptive; the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباساً﴾ a past verb and its two objects, its fāʿil latent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعل; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَجَعَلَ النَّهارَ نُشُوراً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and its two objects; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:48-50.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ بُشْراً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) بشرا. ﴿يَدَيْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: so in the source; the yāʾ of يَدَيْ is the dual ending, and the muḍāf ilayhi of يدي is رحمته.] ﴿رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً طَهُوراً﴾ a past verb, fāʿil, mafʿūl bihi and an adjective (naʿt) qualifying it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزلنا; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the accusative imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and a mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نحيي, and ميتا is an adjective of بلدة; أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to أنزلنا. ﴿وَنُسْقِيَهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the imperfect verb is conjoined to what precedes, accusative, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ ما is a relative noun, genitive by من; the two are attached to نسقيه. ﴿خَلَقْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْعاماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَناسِيَّ﴾ conjoined to أنعاما. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿صَرَّفْناهُ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ attached to صرفناه. ﴿لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of causation, and the imperfect verb is accusative by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كُفُوراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:51-54.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا﴾ لو is a non-jussive conditional particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَبَعَثْنا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of لو, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي كُلِّ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) بعثنا. ﴿قَرْيَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلا تُطِعِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), لا is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿وَجاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهاداً كَبِيراً﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, a mafʿūl bihi, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and an adjective (naʿt) qualifying it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جاهدهم; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the relative is its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and a mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿هذا عَذْبٌ﴾ the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ and عذب is its khabar, and ﴿فُراتٌ﴾ is an adjective; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهذا مِلْحٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿أُجاجٌ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخاً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; بينهما is attached to something omitted in the place of the second object, and برزخا is its first object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَحِجْراً﴾ conjoined to برزخا. ﴿مَحْجُوراً﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ هو is mubtadaʾ and the relative noun is its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿خَلَقَ مِنَ الْماءِ بَشَراً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent and a mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خلق; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾ a past verb, a latent fāʿil, and a first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَسَباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَصِهْراً﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَكانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:55-59.t: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعبدون, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما لا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ ما is a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), لا is negating, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to ما لا ينفعهم. ﴿وَكانَ الْكافِرُ عَلى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ظهيرا, the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ ما is negating, and a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مُبَشِّراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾ conjoined to مبشرا. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ﴾ ما is negating, and an imperfect verb and its object; the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿أَجْرٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as the excepted in a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿مِنْ﴾; the Quranic word is مَنْ.] ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ﴾ أن is an accusative-governing particle, and it together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of شاء. ﴿إِلى رَبِّهِ﴾ attached to يتخذ. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ the first mafʿūl bihi of يتخذ. ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ an imperative whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَى الْحَيِّ﴾ attached to توكل. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ the relative noun is an adjective (naʿt) of حي. ﴿لا يَمُوتُ﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ conjoined to توكل. ﴿وَكَفى﴾ a past verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and the hāʾ is genitive in form, nominative in position, as fāʿil. ﴿بِذُنُوبِ﴾ attached to خبيرا. ﴿عِبادِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَبِيراً﴾ tamyīz (specification).

daas-irab:60-62.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) قيل. ﴿اسْجُدُوا﴾ an imperative and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِلرَّحْمنِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اسجدوا. ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَمَا﴾ the wāw is redundant (zāʾida), and ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿أَنَسْجُدُ﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and the clause نسجد is the object of the speech. ﴿لِما﴾ ما is relative, and the two are attached to نسجد. ﴿تَأْمُرُنا﴾ an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and نا is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَزادَهُمْ نُفُوراً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and a mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿نُفُوراً﴾ is tamyīz (specification); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). [Translator's note: so in the source, which mentions both a mafʿūl bihi and a tamyīz; نفورا is ordinarily taken as the second object of زاد.] ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause جعل is the ṣila. ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾ attached to جعل. ﴿بُرُوجاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها سِراجاً﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَقَمَراً مُنِيراً﴾ conjoined, and منيرا is an adjective (naʿt). ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ خِلْفَةً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and its two objects, النهار being conjoined to الليل; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ من is a genitive relative noun, and the two are attached to جعل, and the clause ﴿أَرادَ﴾ is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by أن, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَوْ أَرادَ شُكُوراً﴾ the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:63-66.t: ﴿وَعِبادُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and عباد is mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is at the end of the sura, namely His words ﴿أُوْلئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ﴾. ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, an adjective (naʿt) of الرحمن, or the khabar of the mubtadaʾ عباد; the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: so in the source, «صفة للرحمن»; the relative الذين qualifies عباد.] ﴿يَمْشُونَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يمشون. ﴿هَوْناً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), or an adjective of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a gentle walking". ﴿وَإِذا﴾ an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿خاطَبَهُمُ الْجاهِلُونَ﴾ a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first and a fāʿil (agent) placed later; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قالُوا سَلاماً﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the preceding الذين. ﴿يَبِيتُونَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾ attached to سجدا. ﴿سُجَّداً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿وَقِياماً﴾ conjoined to سجدا. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رَبَّنَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, muḍāf, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذابَ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and a mafʿūl bihi, and عنا is attached to اصرف. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿إِنَّ عَذابَها﴾ inna and its noun, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كانَ غَراماً﴾ kāna and its khabar, its noun being omitted; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿ساءَتْ﴾ the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَمُقاماً﴾ conjoined to what precedes.

daas-irab:67-69.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the preceding الذين. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا﴾ لم is jussive-governing, and يسرفوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. ﴿وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ conjoined to لم يسرفوا. ﴿وَكانَ﴾ kāna, its noun latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَواماً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لا يَدْعُونَ﴾ لا is negating, and يدعون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb attached to يدعون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آخَرَ﴾ an adjective (naʿt). ﴿وَلا يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined to لا يدعون. ﴿النَّفْسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, adjective. ﴿حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يقتلون. ﴿وَلا يَزْنُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a jussive conditional noun. ﴿يَفْعَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَلْقَ أَثاماً﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent, and a mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من. ﴿يُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, a badal (substitute) for يلق; العذاب is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and له is attached to يضاعف. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to يضاعف. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ﴾ conjoined to يضاعف. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ attached to يخلد. ﴿مُهاناً﴾ ḥāl.

daas-irab:70-72.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā). ﴿تابَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَآمَنَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صالِحاً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and صالحا is an adjective (naʿt); the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَأُوْلئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf is for address. ﴿يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its two objects, accusative by the kasra, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾ kāna, its noun and its two predicates; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمَنْ تابَ﴾ the conditional noun is mubtadaʾ and the clause is its khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and an adjective of a mafʿūl muṭlaq; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is the connective (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun. ﴿يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتاباً﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and a mafʿūl muṭlaq; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتوب; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾ the relative noun is mubtadaʾ, لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil and الزور its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿مَرُّوا﴾ the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ attached to مروا. ﴿مَرُّوا كِراماً﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause has no [grammatical] position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

daas-irab:73-77.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes. ﴿إِذا ذُكِّرُوا﴾ إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition, and a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ذكروا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ذكروا. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها صُمًّا﴾ the imperfect verb is jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and صما is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يخروا. [Translator's note: so in the source; صُمًّا is usually parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial).] ﴿وَعُمْياناً﴾ conjoined to صما; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿هَبْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَنا﴾ attached to هب. ﴿مِنْ أَزْواجِنا﴾ attached to هب, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَذُرِّيَّاتِنا﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿قُرَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَعْيُنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿وَاجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِماماً﴾ a verb of supplication, its fāʿil latent, and its two objects, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] attached to اجعلنا. ﴿أُوْلئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, being its first object, and الغرفة is the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿بِما﴾ attached to يجزون; and the clause أولئك.. is the khabar of عباد الرحمن. ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, and تحية is the second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَسَلاماً﴾ conjoined to تحية. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to خالدين. ﴿حَسُنَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَمُقاماً﴾ conjoined to مستقرا; the clause حسنت is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يَعْبَؤُا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ attached to يعبؤ. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ fāʿil, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the speech. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿دُعاؤُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi, and the khabar is omitted. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿كَذَّبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and سوف is for the future and deferment (tashwīf). ﴿يَكُونُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun omitted. ﴿لِزاماً﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي﴾: a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقانَ﴾: a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى عَبْدِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِيَكُونَ﴾: the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl), and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن, whose noun is omitted. ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نذيرا. ﴿نَذِيراً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of يكون. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: badal (substitute) for the preceding الذي. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿مُلْكُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَلَمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لم makes the verb jussive. ﴿يَتَّخِذْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَلَداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ﴾: an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive by لم; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿شَرِيكٌ﴾: the noun of يكن; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الْمُلْكِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شريك. ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ﴾: a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَقْدِيراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿من دون﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اتخذوا. ﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آلِهَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا يَخْلُقُونَ﴾: لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of آلهة. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَخْلُقُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with active vowelling; the Quranic text is يُخْلَقُونَ, as the parsing indicates.] ﴿وَلا يَمْلِكُونَ﴾: conjoined to يخلقون and parsed like it. ﴿لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يملكون. ﴿ضَرًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلا نَفْعاً﴾: conjoined to ضرا. ﴿وَلا يَمْلِكُونَ مَوْتاً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا حَياةً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا نُشُوراً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, لا is redundant (zāʾida), and نشورا is conjoined.

daas-irab:4-6.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾: negating. ﴿هَذا﴾: the hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿إِفْكٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿افْتَراهُ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible; its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of إفك. ﴿وَأَعانَهُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to افتراه. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعانه. ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿آخَرُونَ﴾: an adjective, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿جاؤُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ظُلْماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَزُوراً﴾: conjoined to ظلما. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾: khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿اكْتَتَبَها﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَهِيَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and mubtadaʾ. ﴿تُمْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بُكْرَةً﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿وَأَصِيلًا﴾: conjoined to بكرة; the clause is the khabar of هي. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ﴾: a past verb and its fronted object; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative [noun], fāʿil. ﴿يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يعلم. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: إنّ and its noun; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no position. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted; the clause is the khabar of إنه. ﴿غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾: the two khabars of كان.

daas-irab:7-9.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِهذَا﴾: ذا is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the lām; [the two are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾: badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيَمْشِي﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يأكل, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِي الْأَسْواقِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يمشي. ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ﴾: a passive past verb, and ملك is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل. ﴿فَيَكُونَ﴾: the fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the causative fāʾ. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to نذيرا; and its noun is omitted. ﴿نَذِيراً﴾: khabar. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يُلْقى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible, and كنز is nāʾib fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يلقى; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تَكُونُ﴾: an incomplete imperfect verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿جَنَّةٌ﴾: the noun of تكون; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَأْكُلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of جنة. ﴿مِنْها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأكل. ﴿وَقالَ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a particle of negation. ﴿تَتَّبِعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رَجُلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مَسْحُوراً﴾: an adjective. ﴿انْظُرْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as ḥāl. ﴿ضَرَبُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of انظر. ﴿لَكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَمْثالَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is negating. ﴿يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:10-12.t: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي﴾: a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿إِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no position. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿لَكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل. ﴿خَيْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْ ذلِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is in the position of genitive by من; [the two are] attached to خيرا; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾: badal (substitute) for خير, accusative (manṣūb) like it, the sign of its accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تجري, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is conjoined to the apodosis, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يجعل. ﴿قُصُوراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِالسَّاعَةِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كذبوا. ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: the lām is a preposition, من is a relative [noun]; [the two are] attached to أعتدنا. ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِالسَّاعَةِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كذب. ﴿سَعِيراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿رَأَتْهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to رأتهم. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of مكان. ﴿سَمِعُوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿تَغَيُّظاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَزَفِيراً﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تغيظا.

daas-irab:13-16.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿أُلْقُوا﴾: a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the statement is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ألقوا. ﴿مَكاناً﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to ألقوا. ﴿ضَيِّقاً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿دَعَوْا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿هُنالِكَ﴾: a demonstrative for place; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address; [it is] in the position of accusative as an adverb. ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿لا تَدْعُوا﴾: لا is prohibitive; تدعوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). [Translator's note: so in the source; تدعوا (a plural verb) is jussive by the dropping of the nūn.] ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to تدعوا. ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿واحِداً﴾: an adjective. ﴿وَادْعُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾: an adjective. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَذلِكَ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿جَنَّةُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذلك. ﴿الْخُلْدِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾: a relative noun, adjective of جنة. ﴿وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿كانَتْ﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters), the tāʾ being for the feminine, and the noun of كان is latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿جَزاءً﴾: the khabar of كان. ﴿وَمَصِيراً﴾: conjoined. ﴿لَهُمْ فِيها﴾: both are attached to the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿ما﴾: a relative [noun], postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَشاؤُنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿عَلى رَبِّكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَعْداً﴾: the khabar of كان. ﴿مَسْؤُلًا﴾: an adjective of وعدا; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "واذكر". ﴿يَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object of يحشرهم. ﴿يَعْبُدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and أنتم is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَضْلَلْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿عِبادِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: the hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and the demonstrative is badal (substitute). ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿سُبْحانَكَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾: negating. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿يَنْبَغِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿لَنا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينبغي. ﴿أَنْ﴾: [a particle] making the verb accusative. ﴿نَتَّخِذَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نتخذ. ﴿مِنْ﴾: redundant (zāʾida). ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾: genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative in position, first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿مَتَّعْتَهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَآباءَهُمْ﴾: conjoined to the object of متعتهم. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive. ﴿نَسُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الذِّكْرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and كان (of kāna and its sisters) and its noun. ﴿قَوْماً﴾: khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بُوراً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of قوما.

daas-irab:19-20.t: ﴿فَقَدْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كَذَّبُوكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause has no position, [being] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿بِما﴾: ما is a relative [noun]; [the two are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبوكم. ﴿تَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negating. ﴿تَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿صَرْفاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿نَصْراً﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to صرفا. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun], mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَظْلِمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نُذِقْهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil is latent; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿عَذاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَبِيراً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَبْلَكَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to أرسلنا, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أرسلنا. ﴿إِلَّا إِنَّهُمْ﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and إنّ and its noun; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لَيَأْكُلُونَ﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿الطَّعامَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيَمْشُونَ﴾: conjoined to يأكلون and parsed like it. ﴿فِي الْأَسْواقِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يمشون. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is conjoined, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيراً﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters), its noun and its khabar, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:21-23.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿لا يَرْجُونَ﴾: لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِقاءَنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾: a passive past verb. ﴿عَلَيْنَا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَوْ نَرى﴾: أو is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَقَدِ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استكبروا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the answer to the oath. ﴿وَعَتَوْا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to استكبروا and parsed like it. ﴿عَتَوْا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). [Translator's note: the source repeats the verb's spelling here; the word parsed is the verbal noun عُتُوًّا.] ﴿كَبِيراً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر". ﴿يَرَوْنَ الْمَلائِكَةَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and الملائكة its object; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation. ﴿بُشْرى﴾: the noun of لا, accusative with an implied fatḥa on the alif because [its pronunciation] is impossible. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to another like it. ﴿لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَحْجُوراً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and محجورا is an adjective. ﴿وَقَدِمْنا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلى ما﴾: the relative noun is genitive by إلى; [the two are] attached to قدمنا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ عَمَلٍ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿هَباءً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of جعل. ﴿مَنْثُوراً﴾: an adjective of هباء, accusative like it.

daas-irab:24-27.t: ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of أصحاب; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to خير. ﴿مَقِيلًا﴾: tamyīz. ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: an adverb, accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "واذكر". ﴿تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْغَمامِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تشقق. ﴿وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿الْمُلْكُ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: يوم is an adverb annexed to an adverb, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of الملك. ﴿لِلرَّحْمنِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَكانَ يَوْماً﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters), its noun being omitted, and يوما is its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عسيرا. ﴿عَسِيراً﴾: an adjective of يوما. ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and يوم is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; the statement is resumptive. ﴿يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى يَدَيْهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يعض. ﴿يَقُولُ﴾: the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يا﴾: for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾: ليت and its noun. ﴿اتَّخَذْتُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of ليت, and the clause of ليت is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مَعَ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), occupying the place of the second object of اتخذت. ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:28-31.t: ﴿يا﴾: for the vocative. ﴿وَيْلَتى﴾: munādā muḍāf (an annexed noun addressed in the vocative), and the yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the yāʾ having been changed into an alif; the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾: ليت and its noun. ﴿لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ليت. ﴿فُلاناً خَلِيلًا﴾: the two objects of أتخذ; the clause ليتني is initial. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَضَلَّنِي﴾: a past verb and its object, its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause has no position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿عَنِ الذِّكْرِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أضلني. ﴿بَعْدَ إِذْ﴾: an adverb annexed to an adverb, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿جاءَنِي﴾: a past verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its fāʿil being latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكانَ الشَّيْطانُ لِلْإِنْسانِ خَذُولًا﴾: the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl, and كان (of kāna and its sisters), its noun and its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خذولا; the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl. ﴿وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يا رَبِّ﴾: يا is a vocative particle; رب is munādā muḍāf, and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّ قَوْمِي﴾: إنّ and its noun, and the yāʾ of the first person is in the position of genitive; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of إنّ. ﴿هذَا﴾: the hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, first mafʿūl bihi of اتخذوا. ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾: badal (substitute). ﴿مَهْجُوراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the kāf is a preposition, and ذا is a demonstrative, genitive by the kāf; [the two are] attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun stand in for the second object of جعل, and نبي is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَدُوًّا﴾: first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عدوا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَفى﴾: a past verb. ﴿بِرَبِّكَ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition; ربك is fāʿil in position, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هادِياً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَنَصِيراً﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to هاديا; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa).

daas-irab:32-34.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb, and the relative noun is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ﴾: a passive past verb, and القرآن is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿جُمْلَةً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿واحِدَةً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): "نزلناه تنزيلا كذلك" (We sent it down in such a sending). ﴿لِنُثَبِّتَ﴾: the lām is for reason (taʿlīl), and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb). ﴿بِهِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نثبت; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿فُؤادَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَرَتَّلْناهُ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to the omitted نزلناه. ﴿تَرْتِيلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿وَلا﴾: لا is negating. ﴿يَأْتُونَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَلا﴾: لا is negating. ﴿يَأْتُونَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and mafʿūl bihi. [Translator's note: the source repeats وَلا يَأْتُونَكَ here and gives no analysis for ﴿بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْناكَ﴾, which the next item presupposes.] ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جئناك; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَأَحْسَنَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الحق, and genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿تَفْسِيراً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُحْشَرُونَ﴾: the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿إِلى جَهَنَّمَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يحشرون. ﴿أُوْلئِكَ شَرٌّ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). ﴿مَكاناً﴾: tamyīz. ﴿وَأَضَلُّ﴾: conjoined to شر. ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: tamyīz; the clause أولئك etc. is the khabar of الذين.

daas-irab:35-37.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿مَعَهُ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَخاهُ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هارُونَ﴾: badal (substitute) for أخاه. ﴿وَزِيراً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَقُلْنَا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿اذْهَبا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِلَى الْقَوْمِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اذهبا. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, adjective (ṣifa) of القوم. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كذبوا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَدَمَّرْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَدْمِيراً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَقَوْمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "وأغرقنا". ﴿نُوحٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَمَّا﴾: an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna), or a conditional particle that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ﴾: the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَغْرَقْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿وَجَعَلْناهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ آيَةً﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلناهم. ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أعتدنا. ﴿عَذاباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَلِيماً﴾: an adjective; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:38-40.t: ﴿وَعاداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر عادا". ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عادا. ﴿وَأَصْحابَ الرَّسِّ وَقُرُوناً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of قرونا. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَثِيراً﴾: a second adjective of قرونا. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb. ﴿ضَرَبْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no position. ﴿لَهُ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ضربنا. ﴿الْأَمْثالَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾: fronted mafʿūl bihi of تبرنا. ﴿تَبَّرْنا تَتْبِيراً﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَتَوْا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أتوا. ﴿الَّتِي﴾: an adjective of القرية. ﴿أُمْطِرَتْ﴾: a passive past verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَطَرَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿السَّوْءِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, meaning the stones; the town is Sodom, the destroyed town of Lot. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr), the fāʾ is resumptive, and لم is a particle making the verb jussive. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the wāw is its noun. ﴿يَرَوْنَها﴾: an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of يكونوا. ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كانُوا﴾: كان (of kāna and its sisters) and its noun. ﴿لا يَرْجُونَ﴾: لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿نُشُوراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause أفلم يكونوا... is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:41-42.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition. ﴿رَأَوْكَ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنْ﴾: negating. ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, fāʿil and first object; the clause has no position because it is the answer of a condition that does not make the verb jussive and is not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُزُواً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of يتخذونك. ﴿أَهذَا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr). ﴿هذَا﴾: the hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿بَعَثَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, with the Name of Majesty as fāʿil. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy [إنّ] (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla). ﴿كادَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿لَيُضِلُّنا﴾: the lām is the lām that distinguishes between negation and affirmation (al-lām al-fāriqa), and an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil being a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is the khabar of كاد. ﴿عَنْ آلِهَتِنا﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يضلنا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a conditional particle that does not make the verb jussive. ﴿أَنْ صَبَرْنا﴾: أن is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and a past verb and its fāʿil; أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is omitted. ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: preposition and its genitive noun, attached to صبرنا; the answer of لولا is omitted, its implied form being "لولا صبرنا موجود لأضلنا" (were it not that our patience existed, he would have led us astray). ﴿وَسَوْفَ﴾: the wāw is for resumption, and سوف is a particle of the future. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿حِينَ﴾: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to يعلمون. ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb and fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾: khabar; the clause is the object of يرون. [Translator's note: so in the source; the interrogative clause is usually taken as the object of يعلمون.] ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾: tamyīz (specification).

farraa:1-1.t: His saying: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ — it is from al-baraka (blessing). In Arabic it is like your saying "Holy is our Lord" (taqaddasa rabbunā). Blessing and holiness [here mean] greatness, and the two are, after all, the same.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْلاۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ﴾ — the answer is with the fāʾ because (لولا) is equivalent to hallā (why not).

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ يُلْقَىٰ إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ﴾ for him — both are nominative, referred back to (لَولاَ), like your saying in speech: "or why is there not cast to him…". It has also been read (نَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا), and (yaʾkulu, with the yāʾ and with the nūn).

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلاً﴾ — He is saying: they cannot find any stratagem in your matter.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِيۤ إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ﴾ — a conditional (jazāʾ). ﴿وَيَجْعَل لَّكَ قُصُوراً﴾ is jussive, referred back to (جَعَل), and (جَعَلَ) has the sense of a jussive. It may also be nominative while being, in that [reading], jussive [in form], because it is a lām that met a lām and so was made quiescent. If you put it in a clear nominative, that is permissible; (and its accusative is permissible by ṣarf (diversion)).

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً﴾ — it is like the fury of a human being when he is angry: his breast boils and it shows in his speech.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾ — al-thubūr is a maṣdar; that is why He said ﴿ثُبُوراً كثيراً﴾ [and not a plural], because maṣdars are not pluralised. Do you not see that you say "I sat a long sitting" and "I beat him a great beating", and do not pluralise? The Arabs say: "What thabaraka from this?", that is, what turned you away from it. It is as though they called out [for destruction] because of what they had done, as a man says: "O my remorse!"

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ وَعْداً مَّسْئُولاً﴾ — He is saying: Allah promised them Paradise, and they asked Him for it in this world when they said ﴿رَبَّنا وآتنا مَا وعَدْتَنَا عَلَى رُسُلك﴾ — He means on the tongues of Your messengers; and on the Day of Resurrection it is not asked for. It may be in speech that you say "I will surely give you a thousand — a promise to be claimed (masʾūl)", that is, it is due to you, so you may claim it; for what is masʾūl is due, even if it is not asked for, like a debt.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ سُبْحَانَكَ مَا كَانَ يَنبَغِي لَنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾ — the idols said: "It was not for us to worship other than You; so how could we call [people] to worship us!" Then they said: "But You, O Lord, gave them enjoyment of wealth and children until they forgot Your remembrance." So Allah said to the humans: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ﴾ — He is saying: ﴿كذَّبتكم الآلهة بما تقولونَ﴾ «[Translator's note: a paraphrase, "the gods have given you the lie in what you say", placed in ornate brackets in the source.]». It is also read ﴿بِمَا يقولون﴾ with the yāʾ (and the tāʾ). Whoever reads with the tāʾ, it is like your saying "He gave you the lie; he gives you the lie"; and whoever reads with the yāʾ says: they gave you the lie by their saying. The Readers are agreed on fatḥa of the nūn in (نَتَّخِذَ), except Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī, who read (أن نُتَّخَذَ) with ḍamma on the nūn ﴿مِنْ دُونِكَ﴾. Had there been no (مِنْ) with al-awliyāʾ, it would be a good way; and despite (its irregularity and) the fewness of those who read it, it may be permissible on the basis that the noun is put in ﴿مِن أوليَاء﴾, even though it occupies the position of the verb [i.e. the predicate] «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 130b]». I preferred the saying of the majority only because the Arabs bring (مِن) into the nouns [i.e. subjects and objects], not into predicates. Do you not see that they say "I did not take anything (min shayʾ)" and "I have nothing (min shayʾ)", but they do not say "I did not see ʿAbdallāh as any man (min rajul)"? But if they meant "I did not see any man (min rajul) [as] ʿAbdallāh", making ʿAbdallāh the predicate, that would be permissible. And that is the view of Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī.
His saying: ﴿قَوْماً بُوراً﴾ — al-būr is a maṣdar, singular and plural alike; al-bāʾir is that which has nothing in it. You say: "Their dwellings became būr", that is, with nothing in them. Likewise the deeds of the unbelievers are void. One says "a būr man" and "a būr people".

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾ — (ليأكلون) is a ṣila (relative clause) of an omitted noun, [its mention] made unnecessary by "of the messengers" (min al-mursalīn); like your saying in speech: "I have not sent to you any of the people except one who indeed obeys you" — do you not see that (إنه ليطيعَكَ) is the ṣila of man? Its implication is permissible, as He said ﴿ومَا مِنَّا إلا لَهُ مَقَام مَعْلومٌ﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is: except one who has a known station; and likewise His saying ﴿وَإِن مِنْكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾: there is none of you but one who will come to it. And had the lām not been an answer to inna, inna would still have kasra, because it is at the beginning [of its clause], since it is a ṣila.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾ — the nobleman of Quraysh would say, of someone beneath him: "This one has become Muslim before me; shall I then become Muslim after him, so that he has precedence?" That is how some of them were tried by others. Allah said: ﴿أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: He is saying: it is this that you see.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا﴾ — they do not fear meeting Us. It is a Tihāma usage: they put rajāʾ (hope) in the place of fear when there is a negation with it. Of that is His saying ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ للهِ وقاراً﴾, that is, you do not fear His greatness. Someone recited to me:
لا ترتجى حينَ تلاقى الذائدا * أسَبْعةً لاقَتْ مَعاً أم وَاحِداً
(She does not fear, when she meets the defender, whether she has met seven together or one.)
He means: she does not fear and does not care. And another «[Translator's note: the source has «وقال لآخر», apparently for «وقال آخر».]» said:
إذا لسعته النحل لم يَرْجُ لَسْعَهَا * وَحَالفَهَا فى بيتِ نُوب عَوَامِلِ
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he stays close to them in a hive of working bees.)
One says nawb and nūb; and one says awb and ūb, from returning. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-nūb are the male bees.
His saying: ﴿وَعَتَوْا عُتُوّاً كَبِيراً﴾ — al-ʿutuww came with wāw because it is an explicit maṣdar. And He said in [Sūrat] Maryam: ﴿أيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ على الرحمن عِتِيّاً﴾. Whoever makes it with wāw makes it a pure maṣdar; and whoever makes it with yāʾ says: ʿātin and [plural] ʿutiyy; when they formed the plural, their plural was built on its singular. It is also permissible for the maṣdar to be with yāʾ, because maṣdars and nouns coincide in this respect. Do you not see that they say qāʿid and "a people quʿūd (sitting)", and "I sat quʿūdan"? Since the two are identical here, in quʿūd, they did not mind their being identical in ʿutuww and ʿutiyy.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ لاَ بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ — the "day" is not attached to "good tidings" (al-bushrā) so as to be put in the accusative by it; rather, you are implying a fāʾ, as in your saying in speech: "As for today, there is no wealth (fa-lā māl)". When you drop the fāʾ, you are implying the like of "today" after lā. Similar to it in speech: "With us there is no wealth": if you meant "there is no wealth with us" and placed "with us" first, it would not be permissible; but if you implied "with us" a second time after "no wealth", it would be sound. Do you not see that you do not say "Zayd — there is no one beating (zaydan lā ḍāriba), (O you)" as you say "There is no one beating Zayd (lā ḍāriba zaydan)"?
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾ — [i.e.] utterly forbidden that they should have good tidings. Al-ḥijr is the forbidden, as you say: "The merchant laid an interdiction (ḥajara) on his slave", and "He laid an interdiction on his family". Someone recited to me:
فهممتُ أن ألقى إليهَا مَحْجَراً * ولَمِثْلُها يُلْقى إِليْهِ المحجَرُ
(I was about to approach her with a forbidden thing — and it is to one like her that the forbidden is approached.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: alqā and ulqā are from laqītu (to meet); that is, through one like her the forbidden is committed.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدِمْنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنْ عَمَلٍ﴾ — [i.e.] ʿamadnā (We turned to), with fatḥa on the ʿayn. ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ هَبَآءً مَّنثُوراً﴾ — that is, void. Al-habāʾ has a long final vowel and is originally without hamza; its diminutive is hubayy, as al-kisāʾ has the diminutive kusayy. But jufāʾ al-wādī (the scum of the valley) originally has hamza; if you form its diminutive you say "this is jufayʾ", like jufayʿ. Every word with a long final vowel, whether from hamza, from yāʾ or from wāw, is formed by analogy with these two.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾ — he said: some of the ḥadīth transmitters hold that the reckoning of people will be finished in the middle of that day, and the people of Paradise will take their midday rest (yaqīlu) in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. That is His saying ﴿خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾. Now the people of kalām (dialectical theology), when a fool and a wise man are together, do not permit saying "This is the more foolish of the two men" or "the wiser of the two men"; they say: we do not say "This is the wiser of the two men" except of two wise men, one of whom is preferred over the other. Yet I have heard the saying of Allah ﴿خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً﴾, where He made the people of Paradise better in abode than the people of the Fire, though there is nothing of good in the abode of the people of the Fire. So recognise from this their error.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلْغَمَامِ﴾ — it is also read ﴿تَشَّقَّقُ﴾ with doubling; al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it (تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ) with the shīn light. Whoever reads tashshaqqaqu means tatashaqqaqu, with doubling of the shīn and the qāf, and assimilated [the tāʾ], as He said ﴿لا يَسَّمّعون إلى الملأ الأعلى﴾. Its meaning — according to what they have mentioned — is: the sky will split open (from the white clouds), then the angels will descend in it. ʿAlā, ʿan and the bāʾ «[Translator's note: the source has «اليَاء» (the yāʾ), evidently for «الباء».]» in this position (have one meaning), because the Arabs say "I shot from the bow (ʿan al-qaws)", "with the bow (bi-l-qaws)" and "on the bow (ʿalā al-qaws)", meaning one thing.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿لَّقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ — it is said [the dhikr is] the Prophet, and it is said: the Qurʾān. There are two views about it.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي ٱتَّخَذُواْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً﴾ — [i.e.] abandoned. It is also said: they made it like raving; the Arabs say (the man hajara) in his sleep when he raves or keeps repeating a word.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً﴾ — He is saying: We made some of every prophet's community harsher towards him than others. The one fiercest in enmity to the Prophet ﷺ was Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً كَذَلِكَ﴾ — it is said that it [كذلك] is part of the saying of the idolaters, that is: why was the Qurʾān not sent down to him all at once, as the Torah was sent down to Mūsā? Allah said: ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلاً﴾ — so that We may make your heart firm by it. He used to send down a verse or two, so that between the revelation of its beginning and its end there were twenty years. ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلاً﴾ — We sent it down piece by piece. It is also said that (كذلك) is from the saying of Allah: their speech ends at (جملةً وَاحِدَةً), and Allah said: Thus have We sent it down, O Muḥammad, in parts, so that We may make your heart firm by it.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيراً﴾ — it is like His saying ﴿أصحابُ الجنَّة يوْمَئِذٍ وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾ in the meaning of the sentence and in the accusative [of the tamyīz, specification].

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَقُلْنَا ٱذْهَبَآ﴾ — in meaning, only Mūsā was commanded to go. This is like His saying ﴿نَسِيا حُوتَهُمَا﴾, and like His saying ﴿يَخرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللؤلؤُ والمَرْجان﴾, when they come out of only one of them. Its matter has already been explained.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُواْ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ — you put them in the accusative by aghraqnāhum, or if you wish by the destruction mentioned before them.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَأَصْحَابَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُوناً﴾ — they are accusative by the destruction. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is said that al-rass is a well.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلاًّ تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيراً﴾ — We destroyed them and annihilated them utterly.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾ — one of them would pass by a fine-looking stone and worship it; that is His saying ﴿ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ﴾ — [this is] what lies between the break of dawn and sunrise. His saying ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِناً﴾ — He is saying: permanent. His saying ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلاً﴾ — He is saying: when there is sun in a place «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 131b]», there was shade in it before that; so the sun was made an indicator of the shade.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً﴾ — He means the shade: when the sun overtakes it, the shade is drawn in an easy drawing-in; He is saying: gentle and imperceptible.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْرَى﴾ — the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (الرياح) in three places: two of them are words in our reading, and one is in al-Naḥl and is not in our reading, in the place of His saying ﴿والنجوم مُسَخرات بأمره﴾; this is one — he means the one in al-Furqān «[Translator's note: the source has «القرقان», a misprint for «الفرقان».]» — and the other is in al-Rūm: ﴿الرياح مُبَشِّراتٍ﴾. ʿĀṣim used to read what was of the wind's mercy as riyāḥ, and what was of punishment he read rīḥ. The Readers differed concerning mercy: some read al-rīḥ and some read al-riyāḥ; but they did not differ about punishment being with al-rīḥ. We think they chose al-riyāḥ for mercy because the winds of mercy come from the east wind (al-ṣabā), the south wind and the north wind, of the three well-known ones; while what most often brings punishment, and has no rain in it, is the west wind (al-dabūr), because the dabūr hardly ever fertilises [the clouds]. So it was called rīḥ, in the singular, because it does not circulate as the fertilising winds circulate.
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ, that they both read (نَشْراً). The Readers have read (نُشُراً) and (نُشْراً), and ʿĀṣim read (بُشراً). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that he read (بُشُراً), as though [from] bashīra, [plural] bushur.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً﴾ — its singular is insiyy; or if you wish you may take it as insān and then form its plural as anāsiyy, so that the yāʾ is a substitute for the nūn. Insān is originally insiyān, because the Arabs form its diminutive as unaysiyān. When they say anāsīn, it is clear, like bustān and basātīn. And when they say (anāsiya kathīran), lightening the yāʾ, they have dropped the yāʾ that comes between the ʿayn and the lām of the word, as in qarāqīr and qarāqir. What shows the permissibility of anāsī, light, is the Arabs' saying anāsiya kathīra; but we have not heard it in the recitation.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً﴾ — al-barzakh is the barrier: He placed a barrier between them so that the salt would not overcome the sweet.
His saying: ﴿وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾ — (of that, that is) utterly forbidden that one of them should overcome the other.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً﴾ — al-muẓāhir is the helper, and al-ẓahīr is help (or a helper).

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ﴾ — they mentioned that Musaylima used to be called al-Raḥmān; so they said: "We know no Raḥmān except the one in al-Yamāma", meaning Musaylima the Liar. So Allah revealed ﴿قُلْ ادْعُوا اللهَ أوِ ادْعُوا الرحمنَ أيَّامَّا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الأسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾.
His saying: ﴿أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا يَأْمُرُنَا﴾ and ﴿وتأمرنا﴾ — whoever reads with the yāʾ means Musaylima; whoever reads with the tāʾ may (also) mean Musaylima, and it would be about the command: "Shall we prostrate to your command to us?" And whoever reads with the tāʾ and the yāʾ, Muḥammad ﷺ is meant by it, (and it is like His saying) ﴿قُلْ للذين كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وتحشرون﴾ and ﴿وسَيُغلبونَ﴾, while the meaning [of the address] is to Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سُرُجاً﴾ — the reading of the general public is ﴿سِرَاجاً﴾. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: [al-Farrāʾ] narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to me from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read (سُرُجاً); and that is likewise the reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh. Whoever reads ﴿سراجاً﴾ refers it to the sun, and that is a good way, because He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجاً﴾. Whoever says ﴿سُرُجاً﴾ refers it to the lamps [i.e. the stars], since one is guided by them; he made them like lamps (suruj), and the miṣbāḥ is like the sirāj in the speech of the Arabs «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 132a]»; and Allah said ﴿المِصْبَاحُ فِى زُجَاجَةٍ﴾.

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ ٱللَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾ — this one goes and that one comes. Zuhayr said about that:
بِها العِينُ والآرام يَمْشِين خِلفَةً * وأطلاؤهَا يَنْهَضْنَ من كل مَجْثَم
(There the wild cows and white gazelles walk in succession, and their young rise up from every resting-place.)
The meaning of Zuhayr's khilfatan is: differing, in that they are of two kinds in colour and form; and khilfa may also be in their gait. It has been mentioned that His saying ﴿خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ﴾ means: whoever misses a deed in the night makes it up in the day, so He made this a replacement (khalaf) for that.
His saying: ﴿لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ﴾ — in the reading of Ubayy it is (يتذكّرَ), which is evidence for whoever reads with doubling. The reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh, of Ḥamza and of many people is (لِمَنْ أَرادَ أنْ يَذْكُر), light; yadhkuru and yatadhakkaru come with one meaning. In our reading there is ﴿واذكُرُوا ما فِيهِ﴾, and in the text of ʿAbdallāh (وَتذكَّرُوا ما فيه).

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾ — Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to me from Jābir al-Juʿfī, from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿اٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾: he said: with tranquillity and dignity.
His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الجَاهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلاَماً﴾ — when the people of Mecca reviled the Muslims, they [the Muslims] would answer them with a fair reply, before they were commanded to fight them.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿ وَالَّذِينَ يِبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِيَاماً﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that whoever recites something of the Qurʾān in prayer, however little, has spent the night prostrating and standing. They mentioned that they are the two rakʿas after the Maghrib, and after the ʿIshāʾ two rakʿas.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً﴾ — He is saying: persistent, permanent. The Arabs say: "So-and-so is mughram with women", when he is infatuated with them; and "I am mughram with you", when one cannot do without the man. We think that the creditor (al-gharīm) was called gharīm only because he claims his due and persists until he receives it.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ﴾ — with kasra on the tāʾ. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿĀṣim read (ولم يُقْتِروا), from aqtartu; al-Ḥasan read (وَلَمْ يَقْتِرُوا), which is from qatartu, like the saying of whoever read yaqturū with ḍamma on the yāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma meant is evidently on the tāʾ (yaqturū).]».
