Whoever says "اَلرَّحْمَنُ", it is nominative (marfūʿ) for one of two reasons. One of them is as a badal (substitute) for what is in His saying ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. the latent pronoun in اسْتَوى], then He made it clear by His saying "اَلرَّحْمَنُ". It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with "فاسْألْ بِهِ" the khabar (predicate); the meaning is: "ask about Him one who is well-informed". Whoever says "اَلرَّحْمَنِ", it is on the meaning of "وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى الحَيِّ الَّذِي لا يَمُوتُ" … "الرَّحْمَنِ", a naʿt (adjective) of "اَلْحَيِّ".

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالُوا وما الرَّحْمَنُ أنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا﴾ — it is also read "يَأْمُرُنا". "اَلرَّحْمَنُ" is one of the names of Allah, mentioned in the earlier scriptures, but they did not know it as one of the names of Allah. So it was said to them: "It is one of the names of Allah": ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَنَ أيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 110]. Its meaning according to the lexicographers is: the Possessor of mercy beyond which there is no further limit in mercy, because "فَعْلانُ" is one of the patterns of intensification (mubālagha). You say "رَجُلٌ عَطْشانُ" and "رَيّانُ" when he is at the extreme of quenched thirst or of thirst; and likewise "فَرْحانُ", "جَذْلانُ" and "خَزْيانُ" when he is at the utmost of joy, or at the extreme of disgrace.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ في السَّماءِ بُرُوجًا﴾: "اَلْبُرُوجُ": it was said they are the great stars. "اَلْبَرَجُ" is a wide space between the eyebrows, and everything that is visible and elevated has "baraja". They were only called "بُرُوجٌ" because of their visibility, their distinctness from one another and their elevation.
﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها سِراجًا وقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا﴾ — it is also read "سُرُجًا", and "سُرْجًا" with sukūn on the rāʾ is permissible, like "رُسُلٌ" and "رُسْلٌ". Whoever read "سِراجًا" meant the sun, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 16]. Whoever read "سُرُجًا" meant the sun and the great stars along with it.

zajjaj:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَن أرادَ أنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أوْ أرادَ شُكُورًا﴾ — it is also read "لِمَن أرادَ أنْ يَذْكُرَ". Al-Ḥasan said: whoever misses his deed of remembrance and thanks has in the night a chance to make amends, and whoever misses it by night has in the day a chance to make amends. The lexicographers said: "خِلْفَةً" means: this one comes in the track of that one; and they recited the verse of Zuhayr:
بِها العَيْنُ والآرامُ يَمْشِينَ خِلْفَةً ∗∗∗ وأطْلاؤُها يَنْهَضْنَ مِن كُلِّ مَجْثَمِ
(In it the wide-eyed wild cows and the white gazelles walk one after another, while their young rise up from every resting place.)
It also came in the exegesis that "خِلْفَةً" means: the two differ from each other, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنَّ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ لآياتٍ لأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 190] ﴿الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيامًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 191], to the end of the verse.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾, that is: they walk with tranquillity, dignity and forbearance. ﴿وَإذا خاطَبَهُمُ الجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلامًا﴾, that is: "we keep ourselves safe from you, a keeping-safe (salāman); we do not behave ignorantly towards you", as though they said: "a dissociation from you". "عِبادُ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The best view is that the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ here is what comes at the end of the sura, in His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الغُرْفَةَ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [al-Furqān: 75], as though He said: "And the servants of the All-Merciful, who have all these qualities…" up to His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إمامًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 74]. It is also possible that His saying "وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with its khabar being "اَلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا".

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وقِيامًا﴾: everyone whom the night overtakes has "باتَ، يَبِيتُ" (spent the night), whether he slept or did not sleep: "باتَ فُلانٌ البارِحَةَ قَلِقًا" (So-and-so spent last night restless). Al-mabīt is simply being overtaken by the night.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّ عَذابَها كانَ غَرامًا﴾: "اَلْغَرامُ" in the language is the severest punishment. The poet said:
وَيَوْمَ النِّسارِ ويَوْمَ الجِفارِ ∗∗∗ كانا عَذابًا وكانا غَراما
(The Day of al-Nisār and the Day of al-Jifār were a torment and were a lasting ruin.)

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّها ساءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا ومُقامًا﴾: "مُسْتَقَرًّا ومُقامًا" are both accusative (manṣūb) as tamyīz (specification); the meaning is: "it is evil in respect of the place of settlement and the place of residence".

zajjaj:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿والَّذِينَ إذا أنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا ولَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾: "يُقْتِرُوا" with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the tāʾ, and with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ; and "لَمْ يُقَتِّرُوا" — but I know of no one who read it so, I mean with a doubled tāʾ. What came in the exegesis is that extravagance (isrāf) is spending in disobedience to Allah, and that there is no extravagance in spending on what brings one closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and everything spent in disobedience to Allah is extravagance, because isrāf is exceeding the limit and the measure. It also came in the exegesis that extravagance is that about which people say: "So-and-so is extravagant". The truth in this is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught His Prophet ﷺ, when He said: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إلى عُنُقِكَ ولا تَبْسُطْها كُلَّ البَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 29].

zajjaj:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أثامًا﴾: "يَلْقَ" is jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The interpretation of الأثام is the interpretation of requital for a thing. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: one says "قَدْ لَقِيَ أثامَ ذَلِكَ", that is: the requital of that. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl hold that its meaning is: "he will meet the requital of sin". Sībawayh said: "يُضاعَفْ لَهُ العَذابُ" is jussive because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting of الأثام, as the poet said:
مَتى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بِنا في دِيارِنا ∗∗∗ تَجِدْ حَطَبًا جَزْلًا ونارًا تَوَقَّدا
(Whenever you come to us — calling on us in our dwellings — you will find thick firewood and a fire blazing.)
because coming is calling on, so he made "تُلْمِمْ" jussive since it has the meaning of "تَأْتِي". Al-Ḥasan alone read "يُضَعَّفْ لَهُ العَذابُ", and it is good and sound; you say "ضاعَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ" and "ضَعَّفْتُهُ". ʿĀṣim read "يُضاعَفُ لَهُ العَذابُ" in the nominative, on the interpretation of its being an explanation of "يَلْقَ أثامًا", as though someone said: what is the meeting of الأثام? and it was said: the punishment will be doubled for the sinner.

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ﴾: it is not that the evil deed itself becomes a good deed; rather the interpretation is that the evil deed is erased by repentance and the good deed is written along with the repentance. As for the disbeliever, Allah nullifies his deeds and establishes the evil deeds against him.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾: it was said: "اَلزُّورُ" is associating partners with Allah. It also came that they do not attend the festivals of the Christians. What came concerning "اَلزُّورُ" is that it is associating partners with Allah. As for the prohibition of false testimony in the Book of Allah, it is His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 36]. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرامًا﴾: its interpretation is: they turned away from it, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 55]. The interpretation of "مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ" is: they passed by everything that ought to be discarded (yulghā), and the meaning of "يُلْغى" is: it is cast aside. It came in the exegesis that when they wanted to mention sexual relations they spoke of it by allusion; and some of them said: it is the mention of obscene talk (rafath), and the meaning is one. It also came that they do not sit with the people of idle talk, who are the people of sins, and do not side with them (yumāliʾūnahum) in them, that is: do not help them in them. It also came concerning "لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ": gatherings of singing.

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ إذا ذُكِّرُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها صُمًّا وعُمْيانًا﴾: its interpretation is: "when they are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping, hearing and seeing what they were commanded and what they were forbidden". The proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنا واجْتَبَيْنا إذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُ الرَّحْمَنِ خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وبُكِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 58]. Similar to this in poetry is his saying:
بِأيْدِي رِجالٍ لَمْ يَشِيمُوا سُيُوفَهم ∗∗∗ ولَمْ تَكْثُرِ القَتْلى بِها حِينَ سُلَّتِ
(In the hands of men who did not sheathe their swords without the slain becoming many by them when they were drawn.)
Its interpretation is: in the hands of men who sheathed their swords only when the slain had become many. The meaning of "يَشِيمُوا سُيُوفَهم" is: they sheathe their swords. So the interpretation is: "and those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, fall down prostrating, obedient".

zajjaj:74-74.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هَبْ لَنا مِن أزْواجِنا وذُرِّيّاتِنا قُرَّةَ أعْيُنٍ﴾ — it is also read "وَذُرِّيَّتِنا". They asked that Allah join their offspring to them in Paradise, and that He make their families such that their eyes are comforted by them. ﴿واجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إمامًا﴾, that is: and make us among those by whom the God-fearing are guided, and who are guided by the God-fearing.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم رَبِّي لَوْلا دُعاؤُكُمْ﴾, that is: were it not for your affirming His oneness. It came in the exegesis: "ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم" means "what would He do with you?". The interpretation of "ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم" is: what weight would you have with Him?! as you say "ما عَبَأْتُ بِفُلانٍ", that is: "he had no weight or worth with me". The origin of "اَلْعِبْءُ" in the language is: the burden; and from that is "عَبَّأْتُ المَتاعَ": I put some of the goods on top of others.
His saying: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزامًا﴾: it came in the exegesis from the group (of exegetes) that the Day of "Badr" is meant by it; and it came that the slain were bound closely together (lūzima) there. It was also read "لَزامًا". Its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: "your denial will be lizām (binding): it will cling to you, so you will not be granted repentance and punishment will cling to you". So the Day of "Badr" enters into this, along with other punishment that clings to them. Abū ʿUbayda said: "لِزامًا" means: a decisive separation (fayṣal), which is close to what we said, except that (our) statement is more explanatory. Abū ʿUbayda recited, from Ṣakhr, the brother of al-Hudhalī:
فَإمّا يَنْجُوا مِن حَتْفِ أرْضٍ ∗∗∗ فَقَدْ لَقِيا حُتُوفَهُما لِزامًا
(If the two escape the death of one land, they have met their deaths inescapably.)
The interpretation of this is that death, when it is decreed, is binding: if one escapes death in one place, it overtakes him in another place, clinging to him inescapably. Whoever read "لَزامًا" with fatḥa on the lām, it is on the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "لَزِمَ، لَزامًا".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Furqān
Meccan
﷽
﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي نَـزَّلَ الفُرْقانَ عَلى عَبْدِهِ﴾ — "تَبارَكَ": its meaning is "تَفاعَلَ" (the pattern tafāʿala) from "اَلْبَرَكَةُ" (blessing); so say the people of the language, and so it was related from Ibn ʿAbbās. The meaning of "اَلْبَرَكَةُ" is abundance in everything possessing good. "اَلْفُرْقانُ" is the Qurʾān; it is called "فُرْقان" because by it a distinction is made between truth and falsehood.
His saying: ﴿لِيَكُونَ لِلْعالَمِينَ نَذِيرًا﴾ — "اَلنَّذِيرُ" is the one who warns of the punishment of Allah; everyone who causes fear has warned. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14].

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظًا وزَفِيرًا﴾, that is: they heard from it the boiling of rage.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿دَعَوْا هُنالِكَ ثُبُورًا﴾ — in the sense of "هَلاكًا" (destruction), and its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as if they said: "ثُبِرْنا ثُبُورًا" (we have been destroyed utterly).

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿لا تَدْعُوا اليَوْمَ ثُبُورًا واحِدًا وادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾, that is: your destruction is greater than that you should call [for it] a single time. It was said "ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا" because "ثُبُورًا" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it serves for little and much in the singular form, as you say "ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا كَثِيرًا" (I struck him much striking) and "ضَرَبْتُهُ واحِدًا", meaning "ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا واحِدًا" (I struck him a single blow).

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ أمْ جَنَّةُ الخُلْدِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾ — if someone says: how can it be said "Paradise is better than the Fire", when there is no good at all in the Fire, and comparison occurs only among things that fall within a single kind? [The answer is that] Paradise and the Fire both fall under the category of abodes, in a single kind; therefore it was said: "أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ أمْ جَنَّةُ الخُلْدِ؟" (is that better, or the Garden of Eternity?), as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 24].

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ وعْدًا مَسْؤُولا﴾ — "مَسْؤُولًا" (asked for): that is the saying of the angels: ﴿رَبَّنا وأدْخِلْهم جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وعَدْتَهم ومَن صَلَحَ مِن آبائِهِمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 8].

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا﴾ — Allah created living creatures and determined for them what sets them right and sustains them, and He determined all of that for His creation with wisdom and measure.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا إفْكٌ افْتَراهُ﴾ — "اَلْإفْكُ" is the lie. ﴿وَأعانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ﴾ — they mean the Jews.
﴿فَقَدْ جاءُوا ظُلْمًا وزُورًا﴾ — "اَلزُّورُ" is falsehood. "ظُلْمًا وزُورًا" is accusative on [the basis of] "فَقَدْ جاؤُوا بِظُلْمٍ وزُورٍ" (they have come with injustice and falsehood); when the bāʾ dropped, the verb reached [the noun directly] and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition).

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿وَقالُوا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — [أساطِيرُ is] the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "and they said: that which is his book is the legends of the ancients", meaning: "of what the ancients wrote down". The singular of "اَلْأساطِيرُ" is "أُسْطُورَةٌ", as you say "أُحْدُوثَةٌ" and "أحادِيثُ".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وأصِيلا﴾ — "اَلْأصِيلُ" is the evening.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا مالِ هَذا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشِي في الأسْواقِ﴾ — "ما" is written separately from the lām. The meaning is: "what is the matter with this messenger, in the state of his eating food and walking in the markets?!" They wanted the messenger to be of other than human constitution, but what is required is that the messenger to human beings be a human being, so that he be closer to being understood.
His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيرًا﴾ — they demanded that there be a partnership in prophethood and that the partner be an angel, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 9], that is: he would not be able to make them understand unless he were a man. The meaning of "لَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not), and the interpretation of "هَلّا" is interrogation; and [فَيَكُونَ] is in the accusative, being an answer with the fāʾ to the interrogation.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿أوْ يُلْقى إلَيْهِ كَنْـزٌ أوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ — and if you wish, "أوْ يَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ". The accusative is not permissible in "يَكُونُ لَهُ", because "يَكُونُ" is conjoined to the interrogation; the meaning is: "why has not an angel been sent down to him, or a treasure cast to him, or a garden be his?" [Translator's note: the source vocalizes «أنْزِلُ» here.] "اَلْجَنَّةُ" is the orchard. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that had He willed that, and better than it, He would have done it, and He said: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي إنْ شاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْرًا مِن ذَلِكَ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ ويَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُورًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 10], that is: had He willed, He would have done more than what they said. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, offered the Prophet ﷺ the matter of this world, but he declined it and preferred the matter of the Hereafter. As for "يَجْعَلْ", it is jussive (majzūm); the meaning is: "if He wills, He will make for you gardens and make for you palaces". Whoever puts it in the nominative does so as a resumption (istiʾnāf); the meaning is: "and He will make for you palaces", that is: "Allah will give you in the Hereafter more than what they said".
His saying: ﴿أوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنها﴾, and "يَأْكُلْ مِنها" [is also permissible].

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ﴾ — [this is] when the angels were asked, and it was said: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أضْلَلْتُمْ عِبادِي هَؤُلاءِ أمْ هم ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾ [al-Furqān: 17]; and it is possible that the address is to ʿĪsā and ʿUzayr. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī alone read: "قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نُتَّخَذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ", with ḍamma on the nūn, as a passive (lit. "that whose agent is not named"). This reading is, in the view of most grammarians, an error. It is an error only because "مِن" enters in this construction only upon nouns when they are the first object; it does not enter upon the object that stands as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [i.e. the second object]. You say "ما اتَّخَذْتُ مِن أحَدٍ ولِيًّا" (I did not take anyone as an ally), but "ما اتَّخَذْتُ أحَدًا مِن ولِيٍّ" is not permissible, because "مِن" enters only because it negates one in the sense of all. You say "ما مِن أحَدٍ قائِمًا" (no one at all is standing) and "ما مِن رَجُلٍ مُحِبًّا لِما يَضُرُّهُ" (no man at all loves what harms him), but "ما رَجُلٌ مِن مُحِبٍّ ما يَضُرُّهُ" is not permissible. There is no valid way for this reading, except that al-Farrāʾ permitted it with weakness, and claimed that he takes "مِن أوْلِياءَ" as the noun (ism) and takes the predicate (khabar) as what is in "نُتَّخَذَ", as if it were made by inversion (qalb). In our view there is no valid way for this at all; were this permissible, it would be permissible in ﴿فَما مِنكم مِن أحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 47] [to say] "ما أحَدٌ عَنْهُ مِن حاجِزِينَ", and this is an error with no valid way. So recognise it, for recognising the error in it is better than reading it; and all the Readers oppose him in this. Of the same kind of slip is in the reading of al-Ḥasan: "وَما تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّياطُونَ".
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَكانُوا قَوْمًا بُورًا﴾ — it was said in the exegesis: "هَلْكى" (perishing). "اَلْبائِرُ" in the language is the corrupt, that in which there is no good; and likewise "أرْضٌ بائِرَةٌ" (fallow land) is land left without being sown.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكم بِما تَقُولُونَ﴾ — it is read "بِما يَقُولُونَ", with the yāʾ and with the tāʾ. Whoever reads "بِما تَقُولُونَ" with the tāʾ, the meaning is: "they have belied you through their saying: that they are gods"; and whoever reads with the yāʾ, the meaning is: "they have belied you through their saying: ﴿سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ﴾ [al-Furqān: 18]". [Translator's note: the explanations of the two readings are given as in the source; one would expect «تَقُولُونَ» to refer to the idolaters' claim and «يَقُولُونَ» to the angels' denial.] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَما تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفًا ولا نَصْرًا﴾, that is: you are not able to avert from themselves the punishment that befalls them, nor to help themselves. [Translator's note: the pronouns shift between "you" and "them" in the source.]

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ إلا إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشُونَ في الأسْواقِ﴾ — this is an argument against them in their saying: ﴿مالِ هَذا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشِي في الأسْواقِ﴾ [al-Furqān: 7]. It was said to them: "Thus were the messengers who passed away: they ate food and walked in the markets; so how could Muḥammad ﷺ be an innovation among the messengers?" As for the entry of "إنَّهم" after "إلّا", it is on the interpretation: "ما أرْسَلْنا رُسُلًا إلّا هم يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ، وإلّا إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ" (We sent no messengers except that they ate food, and except that indeed they ate food). "رُسُلًا" (messengers) was omitted because "مِن" in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ is an indication of what was omitted from it. As for an example of the lām after "إلّا", it is the saying of the poet:
؎ما أنْطَيانِي ولا سَألْتُهُما ∗∗∗ إلّا وإنِّي لَحاجِزٌ كَرَمِي
(The two did not give to me, nor did I ask them, except that I was indeed restraining my generosity.)
He means "أعْطَيانِي" (they gave me). Some grammarians claimed that "مَن" after "إلّا" is omitted, as if the meaning in his view were: "إلّا مَن لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ" (except those who indeed eat food). This is a clear error, because the ṣila (relative clause) of "مَن" would be "إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ", and it is not permissible to omit the relative noun and keep the ṣila.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكم لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً﴾ — there are two views on it. It was said: a nobleman would sometimes want [to embrace] Islam, then learn that someone beneath him in nobility had embraced Islam before him, so he would refrain from Islam lest it be said that someone beneath him had embraced Islam before him. It was also said: the poor man would say, "Why was I not given the station of the rich man?!", and the afflicted would say, "Why was I not given the station of the healthy?!" — such as the blind, the chronically disabled, and those like them. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أتَصْبِرُونَ وكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرًا﴾, that is: will you be patient in affliction? For you have been made aware of what the patient are promised.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْنا المَلائِكَةُ﴾ — the meaning of "لَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not). ﴿أوْ نَرى رَبَّنا لَقَدِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا في أنْفُسِهِمْ وعَتَوْا عُتُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ — so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that those who are not certain of the resurrection, and do not hope for reward for deeds upon meeting Allah, demanded of signs what had not come to any nation among the nations; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they had become arrogant within themselves and been insolent with great insolence. "عُتُوًّا كَثِيرًا" with the thāʾ is permissible. "اَلْعُتُوُّ" in the language is exceeding the limit in wrongdoing.

zajjaj:22-22.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the time in which they will see the angels is the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah has deprived them of glad tidings at that time, and He said: ﴿يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ لا بُشْرى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. "يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ" is accusative in two ways. One of them is in the sense of "لا بُشْرى تَكُونُ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ" (there will be no glad tidings for the criminals on the day they see the angels), and "يَوْمَئِذٍ" is a reinforcement (muʾakkid) of "يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ". It may not be accusative by His saying "لا بُشْرى", because what is connected with "لا" does not govern what precedes it; but when it was said "لا بُشْرى لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ", it was made clear on which day that is, so it is as though it were said: "they are denied glad tidings on the day they see the angels, which is the Day of Resurrection". ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا﴾ — it was also read "حُجْرًا" with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ. The meaning is: "and the angels will say: حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا", that is: "glad tidings are utterly forbidden to them". The origin of "اَلْحِجْرُ" in the language is what you have placed a restriction upon, that is: what you have prevented from being reached; everything you have prevented [access to], you have restricted (ḥajarta ʿalayhi). Likewise the ḥajr of judges over orphans is only their preventing them from disposing of their property; and likewise "اَلْحُجْرَةُ" (the chamber) in which people lodge is what they have enclosed. [The second way:] "يَوْمَ" may be accusative in the sense of "اُذْكُرْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ" (remember the day they see the angels); then He gave a statement and said: ﴿لا بُشْرى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. "اَلْمُجْرِمُونَ" are those who have committed sins, and in this place they are those who have committed disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدِمْنا إلى ما عَمِلُوا مِن عَمَلٍ﴾ — the meaning of "قَدِمْنا" is "عَمَدْنا" and "قَصَدْنا" (We turned to, We proceeded to), as you say "قامَ فُلانٌ يَشْتُمُ فُلانًا" (so-and-so set about reviling so-and-so), meaning "he proceeded to revile so-and-so", and you do not mean "قامَ" in the sense of standing on the two feet. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنثُورًا﴾ — "اَلْهَباءُ" is what comes out of a window-opening with the sunlight, resembling dust. Its interpretation is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, rendered their deeds void until they became like scattered motes. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known the superiority of the people of Paradise over the people of the Fire, and said: ﴿أصْحابُ الجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 24]. "اَلْمَقِيلَ" is the abode at the time of the midday rest; it was also said: it is sleep at midday. It came in the exegesis that the people of Paradise go to their families in Paradise at midday.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ بِالغَمامِ﴾ — it is also read "تَشَّقَّقُ", with the shīn doubled, and the meaning is "تَتَشَقَّقُ" (it splits open). ﴿وَنُـزِّلَ المَلائِكَةُ تَنْـزِيلا﴾ — it came in the exegesis that heaven after heaven will split open and the angels will descend to the earth, and that is His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ والمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾ [al-Fajr: 22].

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿المُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — "اَلْحَقُّ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "اَلْمُلْكُ". Its meaning is that the sovereignty which is truly sovereignty is the sovereignty of the All-Merciful on the Day of Resurrection, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِمَنِ المُلْكُ اليَوْمَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 16], because a passing sovereignty is as if it were not sovereignty. "اَلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقَّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ" (accusative) is permissible, but it has not been read thus, so do not read it. The accusative would be in two ways: one of them in the sense of "the sovereignty on that day belongs to the All-Merciful — I affirm that truly (aḥuqqu dhālika al-ḥaqqa)", and [the other] on [an implied] "أعْنِي الحَقَّ" (I mean: the true one).

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلا﴾ — it is related that ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ is the wrongdoer here, and that he will eat his hand out of regret, and then [it] will grow back. He had resolved upon Islam, and that reached Umayya ibn Khalaf, and Umayya said to him: "My face is forbidden to your face if you embrace Islam — [I will not] ever speak to you." So Umayya refrained from Islam because of Umayya's saying. [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "ʿUqba refrained from Islam because of Umayya's saying".] So when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will eat his hand out of regret and wish that he had believed and taken with the Prophet, upon him be peace, a way to Paradise; and that is His saying: ﴿يا ويْلَتى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أتَّخِذْ فُلانًا خَلِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 28] ﴿لَقَدْ أضَلَّنِي عَنِ الذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إذْ جاءَنِي﴾ [al-Furqān: 29]. It has also been said concerning "لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أتَّخِذْ فُلانًا خَلِيلًا": that is, I wish I had not taken Satan as a close friend; and the confirmation of this view is: ﴿وَكانَ الشَّيْطانُ لِلإنْسانِ خَذُولا﴾ [al-Furqān: 29]. And it is not impossible that his accepting [the advice] from Umayya was of the work of Satan and his helpers. "اِتَّخَتُّ" is permissible, with the dhāl pronounced distinctly or assimilated into the tāʾ, and assimilation is more common and better.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ يا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا﴾ — they made it like "al-hujr"; "اَلْهُجْرُ" is speech from which no benefit is derived, and they used to say that the Prophet ﷺ was talking nonsense (yahjuru). "مَهْجُورًا" may also mean: abandoned, that is: they made it abandoned, not listening to it nor seeking to understand it.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا مِنَ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾ — "عَدُوًّا" is singular in form, and it may carry the meaning of both the group and the individual, as He said: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]; so it may be in the sense of "أعْداءٌ" (enemies). It came in the exegesis that the enemy of the Prophet ﷺ was Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
His saying: ﴿وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ هادِيًا ونَصِيرًا﴾ — "هادِيًا ونَصِيرًا" are both accusative in two ways. One of them is the ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "your Lord suffices in the state of guiding and helping". The second way is that it be accusative as tamyīz (specification), in the sense of "your Lord suffices as guides and helpers".

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً﴾ — its meaning is: "why was the Qurʾān not sent down to him at a single time?" Between the first revelation of the Qurʾān and the last there were twenty years, and they said: why was it not sent down all at once, as the Torah was sent down? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He sent it down in parts so that it would be made firm in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, and He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ﴾, that is: We sent it down thus, in parts; because the meaning of their saying ﴿لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً﴾ indicates the meaning "why was the Qurʾān sent down to him in parts?", so they were informed why that was, that is: for making firm. ﴿وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلا﴾, that is: We sent it down in measured sequence (tartīl), which is the opposite of haste; it is deliberateness.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿إلا جِئْناكَ بِالحَقِّ وأحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا﴾ — its meaning is: "they do not bring you any likeness except that We bring you what is the truth and better in explanation than their likeness", except that "مِن" (than) was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech. If you said "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا، فَكانَ عَمْرٌو أحْسَنَ وجْهًا" (I saw Zayd and ʿAmr, and ʿAmr was better of face), the speech would contain an indication that you mean "than Zayd".

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ إلى جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكانًا وأضَلُّ سَبِيلا﴾ — "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); "أُولَئِكَ" is nominative, a second mubtadaʾ; "شَرٌّ" is the khabar (predicate) of "أُولَئِكَ"; and "أُولَئِكَ" together with "شَرٌّ" is the khabar of "اَلَّذِينَ". It came in the exegesis that people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three kinds: a kind on mounts, a kind on their feet, and a kind on their faces. «It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how will they walk on their faces?! The Prophet ﷺ said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."»

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ وجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أخاهُ هارُونَ وزِيرًا﴾ — "اَلْوَزِيرُ" in the language is the one to whom one has recourse and in whose counsel one finds protection; and "اَلْوَزَرُ" is that in which refuge is sought and by which one holds fast. From it is His saying: ﴿كَلا لا وزَرَ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 11], that is: no refuge and no escape on the Day of Resurrection, except for whomever Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has mercy upon.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَدَمَّرْناهم تَدْمِيرًا﴾ — by it He means Pharaoh and his people, and those who were transformed into apes and swine.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أغْرَقْناهُمْ﴾ — this wording indicates that the people of Nūḥ also belied others besides Nūḥ, because of His saying "اَلرُّسُلَ" (the messengers). It is also possible that by "اَلرُّسُلَ" Nūḥ alone is meant, because whoever belies one prophet has belied all the prophets, since he is opposed to the prophets, because the prophets believe in Allah and in all His messengers. It is also possible that one is meant while the generic term is mentioned, as a man says to a man who spends a single dirham: "أنْتَ مِمَّنْ يُنْفِقُ الدَّراهِمَ" (you are one of those who spend dirhams), that is: one whose spending is of this kind; and "فُلانٌ يَرْكَبُ الدَّوابَّ" (so-and-so rides mounts), even if he rides only one.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعادًا وثَمُودَ وأصْحابَ الرَّسِّ وقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ — "قَوْمَ نُوحٍ" are accusative in the sense of "وَأغْرَقْنا قَوْمَ نُوحٍ" (and We drowned the people of Nūḥ). "عادًا وثَمُودَ وأصْحابَ الرَّسِّ" are accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ and mīm in His saying ﴿وَجَعَلْناهم لِلنّاسِ آيَةً﴾ [al-Furqān: 37]. It may also be conjoined to the sense of ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 37], the interpretation being: "We promised the wrongdoers punishment, and We promised ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of al-Rass". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: and the proof of that is His saying ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 37]. "اَلرَّسُّ" is a well. It is related that they were a people who belied their prophet and threw him into a well, that is: they thrust him into it. It is related that "اَلرَّسُّ" is a village in al-Yamāma called "Malḥ"; and it is related that "اَلرَّسُّ" is the dwellings of a group of Thamūd.
His saying: ﴿وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ — it is related that the span of a qarn (generation) is seventy years.

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الأمْثالَ﴾ — "كُلًّا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "وَأنْذَرْنا كُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الأمْثالَ" (and We warned each one; We struck likenesses for him). ﴿وَكُلا تَبَّرْنا تَتْبِيرًا﴾ — "اَلتَّتْبِيرُ" is destruction and ruin; everything you have broken and crumbled, you have "tabbartahu". From this, broken glass is called "اَلتِّبْرُ", and likewise "تِبْرُ الذَّهَبِ" (gold dust/nuggets).

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أتَوْا عَلى القَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ﴾ — "أتَوْا" (they came), that is: the polytheists of Mecca. By it is meant the town of the people of Lūṭ upon which Allah rained down stones. [Translator's note: the source has «أمَرَ» (commanded), apparently for «أمْطَرَ» (rained).] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that what emboldened them to belie [the truth], and [the reason] that they paid no heed to the punishment they had witnessed in this world, was that they did not believe in the resurrection, and He said: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَها بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا﴾. It was said: [it means] they do not fear the punishment they were promised after the resurrection. But what the people of the language hold is that rajāʾ (hope) is not in the sense of fear — this is the position of those who reject [words having] opposite meanings (al-aḍdād), and it is, in my view, the truth. The meaning is: "rather, they did not hope for the reward of whoever does good after the resurrection, so they committed sins".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا رَأوْكَ إنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إلا هُزُوًا أهَذا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولا﴾ — the meaning is: "they say: is this the one whom Allah has sent to us as a messenger?"

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿أرَأيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إلَهَهُ هَواهُ﴾ — it is related that one of the people of the Jāhiliyya would worship a stone, and when he passed a stone better than it, he would leave the first and worship the second. It was also said: "مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إلَهَهُ هَواهُ", that is: he obeyed his desire and followed it, and did not heed the consequence of that.
His saying: ﴿أفَأنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وكِيلا﴾, that is: a guardian.
